chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, altogether from Ali ibn Mahziyar who said:

Muhammad ibn Hamza al-Ghanawi wrote to me asking me to write to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding a supplication he could teach by which relief is hoped for. So he wrote to me: 'As for what Muhammad ibn Hamza asked regarding teaching him a supplication by which relief is hoped for, say to him: He should persist with: O the One Who Suffices from everything and nothing suffices from Him! Suffice me what is worrying me from what I am in. For I hope that he will be sufficed from what he is in from the sadness, if Allah, the Exalted, wills.'
So I informed him of that, and only a little time had passed until he came out from the custody (prison).

key_terms.يَا مَنْ يَكْفِي مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ: O the One Who Suffices from everything

ai.seo_question: What is the specific supplication for relief from distress taught by Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the efficacy of the specific phrase 'Ya Man Yaku Min Kulli Shay’' as a means of seeking divine sufficiency (Kifayah) for alleviating anxiety and distress. The narrative of Ibn Hamzah’s rapid release from prison serves as a practical testament to the Imam’s teaching, illustrating the immediate spiritual and physical relief granted through sincere reliance on God. This incident underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the power of concise, potent supplications rooted in the Imams' direct instruction.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ali Bin Mahziyar who said,

‘Muhammad Bin Hamza Al-Ghanawy wrote to me asking me that I should write to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> regarding a supplication he<sup>asws</sup> could teach by which the relief could be hoped for’. So he<sup>asws</sup> wrote to me: ‘As for what Muhammad Bin Hamza asked from teaching him a supplication by which the relief can be hoped for, so say to him that he should necessitate (saying of), ‘O the One Who Suffices from everything and nothing suffices from Him<sup>azwj</sup>! Suffice me what is worrying me from what I am in’. Thus, I<sup>asws</sup> hope that he would be Sufficed from what he is in from the sadness, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the Exalted Willing’.
(He the narrator said), ‘So I taught him that, and only a little (time) had come upon him until he came out from the custody (prison)’’.
en.sarwar: 14. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad all from Ali ibn Mahziyar who has said the following: “

Muhammad ibn Hamza al-Ghanawi once wrote to me to ask abu Ja’far (a.s.) to instinct him with a supplication that helps make his wish for relief come true. The Imam wrote back to me, ‘About the request of Muhammad ibn Hamza who wants to be instructed with a supplication that helps make his wish for relief come true, tell him to hold to this: “O the One who suffices for everything and nothing suffices for Him, suffice me in what concerns me in my condition,” 1 hope this will suffice him in his condition of sadness, by the will of Allah, the Most High.’
1 then informed him of the supplication and shortly thereafter he was released from prison.’”
